what: Canadian Pacific Kansas City is the only railway running from Canada through the United States into Mexico. It moves grain, potash, chemicals, cars, energy products and intermodal containers over about 20,000 route miles.
customers: Grain and fertiliser shippers, carmakers, energy and chemical producers, and intermodal logistics companies.
money: chemicals, energy, cars, forest and metal products
containers moving between ports and inland markets
moat: The only single-line rail route linking the three countries of North America, which cannot be duplicated and avoids interchanging freight with another railway.
risks: Mexican trade policy and tariffs directly affect its cross-border advantage
Grain volumes depend on harvests and weather
Debt of about $18 billion remains from the Kansas City Southern merger
Canadian rail labour disputes have halted operations before
opportunities: Cross-border traffic between Mexico and Canada is still being built out after the merger
Companies moving production to Mexico create new freight on its network
Operating margins near 37% are among the best in the industry
watch: Volume growth in cross-border lanes and the operating ratio.
